title: RC 微分电路与积分电路
summary: 同一个方波喂给两条 RC 支路：取电阻电压得到尖脉冲（微分），取电容电压得到三角波（积分）。
description: 两条支路都接在信号发生器（方波 ±2.5 V、500 Hz）和 GND 之间：VIN → C1（10 nF）→ VD → R1（10 kΩ）→ GND；VIN → R2（10 kΩ）→ VI → C2（1 µF）→ GND。CH1 看 VD，CH2 看 VI。

cards.title: 一个方波，两种输出
text: - 信号发生器：方波、**`500 Hz`**、幅度 **`2.5 V`**、偏置 **`0 V`**。CH1 看 VD，CH2 看 VI。
同一个方波进去，两个输出长得一样吗？各像什么？

cards.title: 输出取在谁身上、τ 和半个周期谁长
text: - 两条支路的区别只有两点：输出取在**电阻**还是**电容**上；τ 比半个周期（1 ms）**短得多**还是**长得多**。
- **微分**（取电阻电压，τd = R1·C1 很短）：电容电压不能突变，方波一跳，跳变全落在电阻上；电容很快充好，电阻电压又回到 0。所以 VD 只在输入**变化**的那一刻出现尖峰。
![](fig:diff)
- **积分**（取电容电压，τi = R2·C2 很长）：半个周期里电容只走了指数曲线开头几乎笔直的一段，斜率由输入决定：
$$\frac{dv_C}{dt} ≈ \frac{v_{in}}{R_2 C_2} = \frac{2.5 V}{10 kΩ × 1 µF}$$
- 输入为正时往上爬，为负时往下爬：方波变成三角波。
![](fig:int)

cards.title: 量尖峰和三角波
text: - **`500 Hz`** 时读 VD 尖峰的峰值，和 VI 三角波的峰峰值。
- 把三角波当直线：斜率 = 2.5 V / τi，半个周期 1 ms 走完一个峰峰值。由此反算 τi。
- 最后调到 **`50 Hz`**：半个周期长了十倍，VI 还像三角波吗？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **取电阻电压、τ ≪ 半个周期 → 微分**：只在输入变化时有输出，常用来从方波里取出“边沿”。
- **取电容电压、τ ≫ 半个周期 → 积分**：输出小，形状是三角波。
- **叫不叫微分 / 积分电路，看 τ 和信号周期的比**：同一个积分支路，频率一低就只是普通的充放电。
- **真实电路里**：示波器采样不够快，会漏掉很窄尖峰的最高点，读到的峰值比理想值低一点——这里的仿真示波器也是这样。

caption.text: 虚线：输入方波；实线：VD。每次输入一跳，VD 先跟着跳，然后很快回到 0。

i18n.en: Dashed: the input square wave; solid: VD. At every step VD jumps with it, then quickly falls back to 0.

caption.text: VI（注意纵轴很小）：输入为正时匀速上升，为负时匀速下降——一个小三角波。

i18n.en: VI (note the small vertical scale): rising steadily while the input is positive, falling while it is negative — a small triangle.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: The function generator (already set up) and both scope probes are wired. **Why**: lessons 12 and 13 covered connecting the instruments; this lab is about the circuit's own waveforms. **Your job**: build the two RC branches: differentiator (C1 10nF first, R1 10kΩ to ground, CH1 on R1) and integrator (R2 10kΩ first, C2 1µF to ground, CH2 on C2).
en.title: RC differentiator and integrator
en.summary: One square wave feeds two RC branches: across the resistor you get spikes (differentiator), across the capacitor a triangle (integrator).
en.description: Both branches sit between the generator (square ±2.5 V, 500 Hz) and GND: VIN → C1 (10 nF) → VD → R1 (10 kΩ) → GND; VIN → R2 (10 kΩ) → VI → C2 (1 µF) → GND. CH1 on VD, CH2 on VI.
en.compare:
**Compare**: τd = 10 kΩ × 10 nF ≈ 0.1 ms, τi = 10 kΩ × 1 µF ≈ 10 ms, half a period 1 ms.
- **Differentiator (τd ≪ half a period)**: VD jumps to about ±5 V at every step and decays with τd, back to 0 well within half a period; the peak reads about **4.6 V** (the samples miss the very top). Average ≈ 0.
- **Integrator (τi ≫ half a period)**: VI is a triangle with slope ≈ 250 V/s, Vpp ≈ **0.25 V** (exactly 5 × tanh(T / 4τi) ≈ 0.25 V); τi worked back ≈ **10 ms**.
- **50 Hz**: half a period, 10 ms, ≈ τi; VI becomes an ordinary charging curve, Vpp ≈ **2.3 V**.
hints: Differentiator: C1 first, R1 to ground, VD in between. Integrator: R2 first, C2 to ground, VI in between.
The top of both branches is the generator's red-clip column.
The triangle's slope ≈ input voltage / τi; half a period covers one peak-to-peak.
tests: 500 Hz: VD is positive and negative spikes, average ≈ 0
500 Hz: VI is a small triangle
50 Hz: the integrator condition fails, VI grows

measurements.ask: 500 Hz: CH1 (VD, resistor voltage) spike peak
measurements.explain: The capacitor voltage can't jump, so the whole 5 V step lands on the resistor: ideally about 5 V. The spike loses 63 % in 0.1 ms and the scope's samples miss the very top, so it reads about 4.6 V.

measurements.ask: 500 Hz: CH2 (VI, capacitor voltage) triangle peak-to-peak
measurements.explain: Slope ≈ 2.5 V / 10 ms = 250 V/s; in half a period, 1 ms, it covers about 0.25 V.

measurements.ask: From your peak-to-peak, τi = 2.5 V × 1 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: τi = R2·C2 = 10 kΩ × 1 µF = 10 ms (10.05 ms with the generator's 50 Ω). The integrator's output is small precisely because τi ≫ half a period.
τd = 0.1 ms, so about 0.5 ms after a step it is nearly back at 0: the resistor voltage reflects only the input's **changes**.
choices: during the whole positive half of the input
only for a short time after each step of the input

measurements.explain: Half a period, 10 ms, ≈ τi, no longer τi ≫ half a period: 5 × tanh(0.5) ≈ 2.3 V, an ordinary charge-and-discharge curve.

cards.title: One square wave, two outputs
text: - **Differentiator branch**: VIN → **C1 `10 nF`** → node **VD** → **R1 `10 kΩ`** → GND.
- **Integrator branch**: VIN → **R2 `10 kΩ`** → node **VI** → **C2 `1 µF`** → GND.
- Generator: square, **`500 Hz`**, amplitude **`2.5 V`**, offset **`0 V`**. CH1 on VD, CH2 on VI.
The same square wave goes in. Do the two outputs look alike? What does each look like?

cards.title: Which part you look at, and whether τ or half a period is longer
text: - The two branches differ in just two ways: the output is across the **resistor** or the **capacitor**; τ is **much shorter** or **much longer** than half a period (1 ms).

- **Differentiator** (output across the resistor, τd = R1·C1 short): the capacitor voltage can't jump, so the whole step lands on the resistor; the capacitor catches up quickly and the resistor voltage falls back to 0. VD shows a spike only at the moment the input **changes**.
![](fig:diff)
- **Integrator** (output across the capacitor, τi = R2·C2 long): in half a period the capacitor covers only the nearly straight start of its curve, with a slope set by the input:
$$\frac{dv_C}{dt} ≈ \frac{v_{in}}{R_2 C_2} = \frac{2.5 V}{10 kΩ × 1 µF}$$
- Positive input, it climbs; negative input, it slides down: the square wave becomes a triangle.
![](fig:int)

cards.title: Measure the spikes and the triangle
text: - At **`500 Hz`** read the peak of VD's spikes and the peak-to-peak of VI's triangle.
- Treat the triangle as straight: slope = 2.5 V / τi, and half a period, 1 ms, covers one peak-to-peak. Work τi back from that.
- Finally set **`50 Hz`**: half a period is now ten times longer. Does VI still look like a triangle?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Across the resistor, τ ≪ half a period → differentiator**: output only when the input changes; handy for picking the edges out of a square wave.
- **Across the capacitor, τ ≫ half a period → integrator**: a small output shaped like a triangle.
- **Whether it differentiates or integrates depends on τ against the period**: the same integrator branch is just ordinary charging once the frequency is low.
- **In a real circuit**: a scope that doesn't sample fast enough misses the very top of a narrow spike and reads a slightly low peak — the simulated scope here does the same.

tests.name: 500 Hz：VD 是正负尖脉冲，平均 ≈ 0
50 Hz：积分条件不成立，VI 变大

compare:
**对比**：τd = 10 kΩ × 10 nF ≈ 0.1 ms，τi = 10 kΩ × 1 µF ≈ 10 ms，半个周期 1 ms。
- **微分（τd ≪ 半个周期）**：VD 每次跳到约 ±5 V，再以 τd 衰减，不到半个周期就回到 0；读到的峰值约 **4.6 V**（采样点落不到最顶上）。平均 ≈ 0。
- **积分（τi ≫ 半个周期）**：VI 是三角波，斜率 ≈ 250 V/s，Vpp ≈ **0.25 V**（精确值 5 × tanh(T / 4τi) ≈ 0.25 V）；反算 τi ≈ **10 ms**。
- **50 Hz**：半个周期 10 ms ≈ τi，VI 变成普通的充放电曲线，Vpp ≈ **2.3 V**。

measurements.explain: 电容电压不能突变，方波一跳 5 V 全落在电阻上，理想峰值约 5 V；尖峰 0.1 ms 就衰减掉 63%，示波器的采样点落不到最顶上，读到约 4.6 V。

measurements.ask: 500 Hz：CH2（VI，电容电压）三角波的峰峰值
measurements.explain: 斜率 ≈ 2.5 V / 10 ms = 250 V/s，半个周期 1 ms 走约 0.25 V。

measurements.ask: 用你的峰峰值算 τi = 2.5 V × 1 ms / Vpp
measurements.explain: τi = R2·C2 = 10 kΩ × 1 µF = 10 ms（算上信号发生器的 50 Ω 是 10.05 ms）。积分电路的输出很小，正是因为 τi ≫ 半个周期。

choices: 输入为正的整个半周期
只在输入跳变之后的一小段时间
measurements.explain: τd = 0.1 ms，跳变后约 0.5 ms 就几乎回到 0：电阻电压只反映输入的**变化**。

measurements.ask: 调到 50 Hz：VI 的峰峰值
measurements.explain: 半个周期 10 ms ≈ τi，不再满足 τi ≫ 半个周期：5 × tanh(0.5) ≈ 2.3 V，波形变成普通的充放电曲线。

hints: 微分支路：C1 在前、R1 接地，VD 是它们中间那一点。积分支路：R2 在前、C2 接地，VI 是中间那一点。
两条支路的上端都接在信号发生器的红夹子那一列。
三角波的斜率 ≈ 输入电压 / τi；半个周期走完一个峰峰值。
startNote: **半成品**：信号发生器（已经设好波形）和两个示波器探头已经接好。**为什么**：仪器的接法第 12、13 课练过，这个实验要看的是电路本身的波形。**你要做**：搭两条 RC 支路：微分（C1 10nF 在前、R1 10kΩ 接地，CH1 看 R1）和积分（R2 10kΩ 在前、C2 1µF 接地，CH2 看 C2）。
